answer: Verse alone earns nothing. Each epoch a seat files a sonnet whose last line encodes the solar zenith it measured at noon over its own registered garden, plus the shadow length of a numbered stone in that plot. Models pour out sonnets by the thousand, but zenith and shadow drift with latitude, date and morning haze, so payloads cannot be pre-mined or forged. Two seats filing one garden return identical readings, a collision that slashes both bonds. Faking an identity costs a real plot, a stone, an inclinometer and a witness at solar noon daily: linear, non-rentable, above one seat's yield.
